description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a world-renowned Indian curry featuring tender chicken pieces bathed in a rich, creamy tomato sauce. Its mild yet complex flavors, derived from aromatic spices and a touch of butter, make it a comforting and irresistible dish. This classic recipe promises an authentic taste of India, perfect for a special meal or a cozy dinner.

ingredients.notes: soaked in hot water for 15 min, then drained

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Mix well to ensure all chicken is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove cooked chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 1 tablespoon butter. Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onions and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Saute for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Mixture
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, cumin powder, coriander powder, 1/2 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder (adjust to your spice preference), and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Add the soaked cashews. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down. Stir occasionally.

instructions.title: Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods (if you prefer a smoother gravy). Carefully transfer the tomato mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. If too thick, add a splash of water or chicken stock to reach desired consistency. Strain the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra smooth texture, pressing solids with a spoon.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Return the blended gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces and bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, the sugar, and the heavy cream. Cook for another 5 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors and the sauce to thicken slightly. Crush the Kasuri Methi between your palms and stir into the curry. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with basmati rice, naan bread, or roti for a complete and satisfying Indian meal. Enjoy your homemade Classic Butter Chicken!

tips: For truly tender chicken, marinate overnight. The yogurt helps to tenderize the meat and infuse it with flavor.
Do not skip blending and straining the gravy. This step is crucial for achieving the signature silky-smooth texture of authentic Murgh Makhani.
Always add Kasuri Methi and heavy cream at the very end of cooking. This preserves their delicate flavors and prevents the cream from splitting.
article:
Butter Chicken, known in its authentic form as Murgh Makhani, stands as a crowning jewel in the vast and vibrant tapestry of Indian cuisine. This iconic dish, celebrated for its rich, creamy texture and tantalizingly complex flavors, has captivated palates worldwide, cementing its status as a global comfort food. Originating from the bustling kitchens of Delhi in the mid-20th century, Murgh Makhani offers a harmonious blend of smoky, tender chicken enveloped in a luscious tomato-based sauce. Whether you’re a seasoned chef or a home cook eager to explore Indian flavors, mastering this classic dish is a deeply rewarding culinary journey.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Murgh Makhani, literally translating to "butter chicken," is a dish steeped in culinary history, born from innovation and a desire to utilize leftover tandoori chicken. Its creation is widely attributed to Kundan Lal Gujral at the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, who sought to create a sauce that would keep tandoori chicken moist and flavorful. The result was a revelation: succulent pieces of chicken, traditionally marinated in yogurt and spices and then cooked in a tandoor (clay oven), are simmered in an exquisitely rich gravy.

The hallmark of authentic Butter Chicken is its velvety smooth, slightly sweet, and tangy tomato sauce, infused with aromatic spices like garam masala, fenugreek (kasuri methi), and a generous amount of butter and cream. Unlike many fiery Indian curries, Murgh Makhani offers a milder, more approachable spice profile, making it a favorite for all ages. The interplay of smoky chicken, sweet tomatoes, and luxurious dairy creates an unparalleled depth of flavor that is both comforting and sophisticated.

## Ingredients for Classic Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken at home requires a thoughtful selection of ingredients. The quality of each component contributes significantly to the final taste and texture.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain whole milk yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   1 teaspoon salt

**For the Makhani Sauce:**
*   2 tablespoons ghee or unsalted butter
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes (or 4-5 fresh ripe tomatoes, pureed)
*   1/2 cup raw cashews, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes (optional, but recommended for creaminess)
*   1-2 green chilies, slit (optional, adjust to taste)
*   1 tablespoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), lightly toasted and crushed
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri or regular)
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances acidity)
*   1 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, plus extra for garnish
*   1/4 cup water (as needed for blending/sauce consistency)

**For Garnish:**
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Butter Chicken

Making classic Butter Chicken is a multi-step process, but each stage is straightforward and contributes to the dish's incredible flavor.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients (yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, lemon juice, salt). Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for deeper flavor and tenderness.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter in a large skillet or non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through. The chicken doesn't need to be fully charred like tandoori, but a nice sear adds flavor. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter. Add the chopped onions and sauté over medium heat until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Simmer the Sauce:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews (drained), red chili powder, and garam masala. Add 1/4 cup of water. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down.

5.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an ultra-silky restaurant-style texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step is optional but highly recommended to remove any fibrous bits.

6.  **Finish the Makhani Sauce:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium-low heat. Stir in the crushed kasuri methi, sugar, and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.

7.  **Combine and Enrich:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering sauce. Stir gently to coat the chicken. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the sauce's flavors. Finally, stir in the heavy cream. Heat through gently for 1-2 minutes, but do not boil after adding the cream, as it can curdle.

8.  **Serve:** Your homemade Butter Chicken is now ready. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro and an optional swirl of extra cream.

## Pro Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani

Achieving restaurant-quality Murgh Makhani at home is entirely possible with a few expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse deep flavor. Longer is always better.
*   **Don't Overcook Chicken Initially:** The chicken will finish cooking in the sauce, so aim for just cooked through and nicely seared in the first step. This prevents dry chicken.
*   **Blend Until Silky:** For that signature smooth texture, blend the sauce base thoroughly. Straining it through a fine-mesh sieve afterward is the secret to a truly luxurious mouthfeel.
*   **Toast Kasuri Methi:** Lightly toasting the dried fenugreek leaves in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing them between your palms intensifies their unique, slightly bitter, aromatic flavor, which is crucial for authentic Murgh Makhani.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste your sauce and adjust. A touch of sugar helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes, while salt enhances all the other flavors. Don't be afraid to add a tiny bit more butter or cream at the end for extra richness.
*   **Resting Improves Flavor:** Like many curries, Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day after the flavors have had more time to meld and deepen.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

The ideal accompaniments for Butter Chicken enhance its rich flavors and provide a complete culinary experience.

*   **Indian Breads:** Warm naan bread (garlic naan or butter naan are excellent choices), tandoori roti, or paratha are perfect for scooping up every last drop of the luscious sauce.
*   **Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a neutral base that beautifully complements the curry's richness.
*   **Sides:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, and onion with a lemon dressing) offers a refreshing contrast. A cooling raita (yogurt dip) can also balance the richness. Pickled onions add a tangy crunch.

## Variations and Substitutions

While classic Butter Chicken is a beloved staple, it's also a versatile dish that can be adapted to various dietary needs and preferences.

*   **Vegetarian Alternatives:** For a delicious vegetarian version, substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese) for Paneer Makhani, or firm tofu. Mixed vegetables like cauliflower, peas, and potatoes can also be used.
*   **Dairy-Free Options:** To make Murgh Makhani dairy-free, use a plant-based yogurt for the marinade, coconut oil or vegetable oil instead of ghee/butter, and full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream instead of heavy cream.
*   **Spice Level Adjustment:** For more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or green chilies. For a milder dish, reduce them or omit the green chilies entirely. Kashmiri red chili powder provides vibrant color with less heat.
*   **Nut-Free Version:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews. To maintain thickness, you can add a tablespoon of poppy seeds (soaked and blended) or a small amount of cornstarch slurry at the end.
*   **Cooking Methods for Chicken:** If you don't want to pan-fry, you can grill, broil, or bake the marinated chicken until cooked and slightly browned.

This comprehensive guide to classic Butter Chicken provides everything you need to recreate this beloved Indian dish in your own kitchen. Its irresistible combination of tender chicken and creamy, aromatic sauce promises a truly satisfying meal that will transport your taste buds straight to the heart of India. Enjoy the process, savor the aromas, and delight in the rich flavors of your homemade Murgh Makhani.
